positive.prompt: Translate these approved business rules into Rust phantom types, sealed traits, and typestate transitions to enforce spec compliance at compile time.
Anchor our state machine transitions into Rust typestate so the compiler prevents illegal workflow steps.
Create a type-anchored spec with sealed traits and opaque newtypes for this sensitive domain value.

negative.prompt: Author an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) capturing our accepted persistence model and system invariants upfront.
Design ownership-safe Rust lifecycles for resources, state transitions, staged startup, and fallible cleanup.

evals.prompt: Given our approved order flow (Draft -> Validated -> Paid -> Shipped), design a Rust type-layer specification using typestate and phantom types.
evals.expected_output: A type-anchored specification template defining state types, consuming transition methods, sealed traits, and closed domain error enums.
expectations: Uses phantom types or typestate for ordered state transitions
Enforces transitions via consuming methods without public bypass constructors
Keeps application logic out of the spec-layer design
prohibitions: Do not implement full runtime application logic
Do not call unwrap() or expect() in spec definitions
